symptom: Executing `describe snippet` output re-binds the snippet's own parameter: TestApp WorkflowCommons snippets come back with a dynamic-text `{1} = $WorkflowUserTask.Name` in the PageParameter slot of its Forms$PageVariable (SnippetParameter emptied), `{1} = $WorkflowUserTask.State` (an enumeration) rewritten as Expression `toString($WorkflowUserTask/State)` with AttributeRef/SourceVariable dropped, and `dataview (DataSource: $WorkflowUserTask/System.WorkflowUserTask_Workflow)` described as `$currentObject/...` so its SourceVariable is dropped. mx check and the build stay green (ako/mxcli#721 L3).
cause: Three sites each knew only the page case. (1) resolveTemplateAttributePathFull never set ClientTemplateParameter.SourceVariableKind, so the writer's sourceVariableToGen defaulted to PageParameter; the flow-argument classifier (#1140) already chose the slot from pb.isSnippet + paramScope. (2) Its `$param.Attr` branch still wrapped a non-String attribute in toString(), the half ledger #76 deferred. (3) associationSourcePath read SourceVariable.PageParameter only, and both association writers (dataViewContextAssociationSourceToGen, associationSourceToGen) hard-coded SetPageParameterQualifiedName; pages.AssociationSource had no snippet flag while DataViewSource did.
file: mdl/executor/cmd_pages_builder_v3.go (resolveTemplateAttributePathFull, parameterSlotKind, buildDataSourceV3 association case); mdl/executor/cmd_pages_describe.go (associationSourcePath); mdl/backend/modelsdk/widget_write.go (associationContextVariableToGen); sdk/pages/pages_datasources.go (AssociationSource.IsSnippetParameter)
insight: Forms$PageVariable has three slots (PageParameter, SnippetParameter, LocalVariable) and every reader and writer of it has to choose one; grep for SetPageParameterQualifiedName / "PageParameter" finds the sites that silently assume a page. The per-document bsonDiff in the round-trip harness truncates at 15 paths and 60 chars, which hid the slot name inside `{"$ID":…` — dumping untruncated diffs (RT_DUMP locally) was what separated this class from L4/L5 in the same documents.
